Plot a TITE-BOIN Decision Table

Source: R/plot.tite_boin_decision_table.R
plot.tite_boin_decision_table.Rd

Draw the decision table produced by tite_boin_decision_table as one panel per number of patients treated. Within a panel, each cell is a pair of pending patients and DLTs, colored by its decision and labeled with the decision code and, where the decision depends on the follow-up of the pending patients, the boundaries on the follow-up statistic.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'tite_boin_decision_table'
plot(
  x,
  n = NULL,
  cohort_size = NULL,
  text_size = 1,
  colors = NULL,
  digits = 2,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

An object of class tite_boin_decision_table.

n

Integer vector or NULL. Numbers of patients treated to draw, one panel each. Defaults to every number in the table.

cohort_size

Integer scalar or NULL. When supplied, only the numbers of patients that are multiples of cohort_size are drawn.

text_size

Numeric scalar. Multiplier applied to every text size in the figure. Defaults to 1.

colors

Named character vector of six colors, with names "E", "S", "D", "DE", "SUS" and "Depends", the last for the states whose decision depends on the follow-up statistic. Defaults to the palette of plot.boin_decision_table extended with gray for suspension and a pale violet for the follow-up dependent states.

digits

Integer scalar. Number of decimal places of the boundaries in the labels. Defaults to 2.

...

Further arguments, currently ignored.

Value

A ggplot2 object, which can be printed, saved with ggplot2::ggsave() or extended with further layers.

Details

A cell whose decision depends on the follow-up statistic shows its codes over the boundaries, kept short so that they fit in the cell. A label such as "E/S" over ">=2.15" means that the dose is escalated when the statistic is at least 2.15 and kept otherwise, and "S/D" over "<=0.52" that it is de-escalated when the statistic is at most 0.52. The boundary marked ">=" always belongs to the first code, which is "E", or "SUS" when escalation is blocked, and the one marked "<=" to "D". The statistic is STFT for method = "imputation" and ESS for method = "ess".

When the table was built with a positive min_follow_up, the code of a cell whose escalation also requires the shortest follow-up of the pending patients to reach that fraction of the window is marked with an asterisk, as in "E*" or "E/S*", and a caption explains the mark.

Every cell carries its decision code, so the figure does not rely on color alone. With many panels, or many patients per panel, the cells become small; draw fewer panels through n, enlarge the figure, or lower text_size. Requires the ggplot2 package, which is only suggested by simFastBOIN rather than required.

See also

tite_boin_decision_table, print.tite_boin_decision_table

Examples

decisions <- tite_boin_decision_table(target = 0.2, max_n = 15)

plot(decisions, n = c(9, 12, 15))


# Every cohort end, with smaller text
plot(decisions, cohort_size = 3, text_size = 0.8)
